### Week 1 Readings

1.  [**The Scientific Method in Five Easy Steps**](https://catterson.github.io/ystats/chapters/1R_WhyStats.html#part-3-how-science)**.** It is the same thing you did in science fair, but with more math. A quick overview, with some deeper thoughts about how to develop a research question that you care about. Please also [read the section on "MeSearch" in Part 2](https://catterson.github.io/ystats/chapters/1R_WhyStats.html#critical-and-culture-in-statistics) (but you can skip the other stuff.)
2.  [**The Goldacre (2010) Chapter from “Why Clever People Believe Stupid Things”**](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/mev9u3oyacrf21dvu48ac/Goldacre_2010_Chapter10.pdf?rlkey=vrcqb617zde7mye8un2xm184k&dl=0)**.** Read the section on "Patterns in Randomness" and at least one other cognitive bias. Some of these biases can be confusing - okay to use other sources or AI tools to help you understand, but let us know if you do!
3.  [**The Replication Crisis in Psychology**](https://nobaproject.com/modules/the-replication-crisis-in-psychology)**.** Focus on the definition of a replication, the reasons for non-replications, and some of the potential solutions to the problem.
4.  **OPTIONAL READINGS :** for those who would like to learn more. Let me know if you find other cool readings on these topics to add.
    - [**More on the replication crisis in psychology**](https://www.vox.com/future-perfect/21504366/science-replication-crisis-peer-review-statistics). The article is now behind a paywall...but [here's a PDF of the article from the Internet Archive](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/21h3kcq6kc5jszo00fm6w/1_Vox_ReplicationCrisis_2020.pdf?rlkey=qzf44rviccwt2ucwvpo86p8ie&dl=0).

### Week 1 Discussion

**YOUR POST :** Use the readings to answer the following questions. Answer these questions on the Vision Board for Week 2. There's no word count requirement; good to be concise.

1.  Think about the research question you identified in class. What past experiences influenced your choice of this topic? Do you think it's possible to be "objective" about this topic?

2.  Summarize one bias from the Goldacre reading [in your own words]{.underline}. And then think of a real-life example of where this bias might apply.

3.  Ask AI (or a real-life human friend) to explain this cognitive bias and give an example in less than 100 words. Paste the response here (and let us know which tool you used). Did AI seem to get this right?

4.  How did the replication crisis in psychology make you feel (in a few words)? Had you heard about this before? What other questions do you have?

**REPLY TO ANOTHER STUDENT'S POST :** Choose another person in the class who doesn't already have a reply.

- Say "hello!"

- What is your own personal connection to the student's research topic? What seems different, what seems the same? Do you think your personal experiences might influence the way you study this topic?
